newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Rail action slows Australian grain movements.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Rail action slows Australian grain movements.

text.p: A 24-hour ban on rostering locomotives for grains shipments in the Australian state of New South Wales that ended earlier on Tuesday caused only "minor disruptions" to wheat shipments, a spokesman for the state's transport system, Freight Corp, said on Tuesday.

The industrial action meant that some trains could not be dispatched from wheat growing regions of New South Wales for delivery to silos in the ports of Newcastle and Port Kembla, the spokesman told Reuters.
"Normally between 10,000 and 15,000 tonnes of grain is shipped to each of the ports daily," he said.
"Yesterday (Monday) that was probably a little less."
However, some trains were already prepared for tipping into silos at the ports, which minimised the impact of the ban, he said.
Grains traders said there was concern that some growers may not be able to ship their wheat, creating a backlog of wheat unable to be placed on freighters for export.
The implications of a backlog would be exacerbated by tight availability of freighter space and Australia's bumper wheat harvest, expected to approach 22 million tonnes this year, the spokesman said.
